subject.title: fix(agents): repair double-escaped JSON strings in tool call argument…

question: Should OpenClaw globally rewrite matching parsed tool-call strings for every provider, or keep this repair constrained to a proven provider/runtime contract while the cross-provider root cause is established?
rationale: The tests and live run support the reported symptom, but they do not establish that every provider emitting the matching sequence is malformed rather than intentionally requesting literal escape bytes.

options.title: Constrain activation to proven inputs
options.body: Gate the repair at the provider or decoded-stream boundary that can be shown to produce the malformed representation, then add coverage for both repaired and untouched paths.

options.title: Accept global heuristic repair
options.body: Keep all-provider activation and explicitly accept the compatibility risk after confirming that preserving literal escape bytes is not a supported tool-argument use case.

recommendation.title: Constrain activation to proven inputs
recommendation.body: Gate the repair at the provider or decoded-stream boundary that can be shown to produce the malformed representation, then add coverage for both repaired and untouched paths.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the adjacent malformed-argument repair and are the strongest available history-based routing candidate for its activation contract.
